design_note: Use derivation records to identify what a forgetting operation must revisit. The example distinguishes a removed source, a surviving embedding and a mixed summary without incorrectly deleting an independent supporting record.

source.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
source.concept: Provenance can record which entities were derived from other entities and which activities produced them, enabling dependency analysis across representations.
source.scope: Original ShopAssist forgetting policy uses derivation metadata to find copies. PROV describes provenance; it does not perform deletion or prescribe this retention policy.

lesson.title: Deleting a note leaves a lineage question
lesson.intro: A user withdraws preference M-31. ShopAssist policy removes its derivatives and rebuilds mixed summaries while retaining unrelated records. Inspect the fictional lineage report before declaring the operation complete.

claims.text: Deleting M-31 removed all of its derivatives.
Summary S-44 needs removal or recomputation.
Independent note M-42 must also be deleted.

sources.text: M-31 is deleted; embedding E-31 derived from M-31 remains stored.
S-44 derives from M-31 and independently retained note M-42.
M-42 came from a separate statement; it was not derived from M-31.

data.verdict: Suppress derived recall; remove E-31; rebuild or remove S-44.

read: L1 exposes a surviving stored derivative even though the source is gone.
L2 identifies the summary that needs cleanup under the stated product policy.
L3 does not establish a reason to delete independent M-42.
lesson.question: Can deleting M-31 alone justify a completed-forgetting status under this policy?
lesson.answer: No. E-31 remains stored, and S-44 still derives from the withdrawn preference. Suppress affected recall while cleanup removes E-31 and rebuilds or removes S-44. Verify that work before marking completion. The lineage does not itself require deleting the unrelated M-42 record.
lesson.takeaway: Follow derivation links to clean up copies without confusing shared use with shared origin.
lesson.assumption: Fictional complete lineage and product policy with no retention exception. Provenance locates dependencies; a separate deletion workflow must suppress and remove them.
